summary: The capability 'Check whether Settlement Date is null for settled transactions' is a single, rule-based completeness test with a binary, reproducible outcome. It needs no judgement, interpretation or reasoning over ambiguous evidence, so it does not warrant an agent. Classified as a Deterministic process; verdict is cut as a standalone agent (implement as a deterministic data-quality check). The only parts needing judgement sit outside the check itself: the approved definition of 'settled', any tolerance/threshold for nulls, and triage of failures. Those remain human decisions or belong to existing candidate roles. Draft only; pending Agent Risk & Governance Reviewer challenge and human sign-off. No draft Agent Contract is produced because none is warranted.
justification: Design principle 9 (avoid creating agents when deterministic automation is more appropriate) applies directly: the check is 'WHERE settlement status = settled AND settlement date IS NULL', a rule whose result does not depend on interpretation. HANDOFF.md also states 'Do not create an agent because a task sounds intelligent' and 'Choose the least complex implementation that is safe and effective'. Principle 10 (keep the agent set as small as possible) reinforces the cut: a dedicated agent for one null check would add to the agent set with no separation-of-concerns benefit. Principle 6 (minimum permissions) and principle 7 (read-and-recommend first) are consistent with a read-only deterministic test and need no agent-level tool grants. The candidate Data Quality Agent already lists 'propose deterministic test' and 'generate candidate SQL' as responsibilities, so any AI involvement in authoring the rule or its SQL would fall inside that candidate's remit rather than a new agent. This overlap is surfaced for human/orchestrator decision and is not merged by this agent. Judgement-bearing elements stay human: the approved meaning of 'settled' (principle 2, agents must not invent definitions) and any null-tolerance threshold (HANDOFF.md decision model lists quality thresholds as requiring human approval). Because the capability is not an agent, the self-necessity rule is not engaged by this verdict.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: 'settled transactions' means rows carrying a settlement-status indicator whose meaning is already defined; this repository evidence does not define it, so the predicate cannot be written precisely until an approved definition is supplied.
ASSUMPTION: the request asks for a repeatable completeness check (count/list of violating rows), not for diagnosis of why nulls occur.
ASSUMPTION: the check would run read-only against a governed dataset; no production data access was requested or granted in this run.

open_questions: What is the approved business definition of 'settled' for this population, and which field or status value encodes it? Human owner (Data Steward / Data Owner) must supply or confirm; this agent will not invent it.
Is zero nulls the expectation, or is a tolerance acceptable? Any threshold is a quality threshold and requires human approval per the decision model.

Which dataset(s) and source system(s) does the check apply to, and is a null-like placeholder (blank string, sentinel date such as 1900-01-01) also to be treated as missing? Not determinable from the evidence available.
Where should the check live (existing DQ tooling, a scheduled SQL test, or a rule in a data-platform or BI tool) and who owns the control? Not determinable from the evidence available.

Overlap to surface for human/Orchestrator decision: the candidate Data Quality Agent already covers proposing deterministic tests and candidate SQL. Should this check be authored through that candidate once it is approved, or as a plain scripted control with no agent involvement? Not merged here.
Does the current registry (docs/CAPABILITY-CLASSIFICATION.md, not read in this run) already contain or classify an equivalent capability? Must be checked by a reviewer with registry access.
recommendations: Do not create an agent for this capability; implement it as a deterministic, read-only data-quality rule (a single null-completeness test scoped to the approved 'settled' population) with a clear owner.
Obtain the approved definition of 'settled' and of the Settlement Date field from the Data Steward / Data Owner before the rule predicate is finalised, rather than inferring either.
Have a human decide whether zero nulls or a tolerance applies; record the threshold as a human-approved value, not an AI output.

Where an agent adds value, keep it downstream of the deterministic check: when the rule fails, exception clustering and root-cause hypothesis generation belong to the candidate Exception & Root-Cause Agent, and mapping questions to the Mapping & Lineage Agent. Those are separate capabilities to be classified on their own request.
Route this Draft to the Agent Risk & Governance Reviewer via the Orchestrator or a human; this agent does not invoke the reviewer directly.

Evaluation-outline pointer: what most needs testing is not the null check itself but whether any downstream consumer wrongly treats it as an agent task or silently supplies its own definition of 'settled'. Test mainly that the control uses only the human-approved definition, that missing or ambiguous definitions cause escalation rather than invented ones, that edge cases for null-like placeholders are handled as an explicit decision rather than a guess, and that threshold decisions are routed to a human. The enumerated Evaluation Scenarios are for the Agent Evaluation Designer to author.

Agent Risk & Governance Reviewer plus a human sign-off: independently challenge this Draft; it is not approved.
